'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Odesa strikes (2022–present)|Odesa strikes]]
***[[Russia]] fires two [[ballistic missile]]s at the [[Port of Odesa|seaport]] in [[Odesa]], [[Ukraine]], for the second time in 24 hours, killing two people and injuring seven others. [https://kyivindependent.com/russia-strikes-odesa-port-with-ballistic-missiles-kills-1-injures-8/ (''The Kyiv Independent'')] [https://www.kyivpost.com/post/53276 (''Kyiv Post'')]
**Fifteen civilians are injured in a nighttime [[Russia]]n [[drone warfare|drone]] and missile attack. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/may/24/russia-drone-attack-kyiv-ukraine-war (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip]]
***At least 79 [[Palestinians]] are killed by [[Israel]]i airstrikes on the [[Gaza Strip]], including nine of a doctor's ten children. [https://apnews.com/article/gaza-israel-palestinians-war-news-8c3fe634bd81986249a235ad53a9044c (AP)]
*[[Naxalite–Maoist insurgency]]
**[[Jharkhand Police|Police]] in [[Jharkand]], [[India]], confirm the deaths of two top [[Naxalism|Naxal]]-[[Maoist]] militants in an operation in [[Latehar]] amid intensified efforts by the [[Indian government]] to end the decades-long Naxal insurgency in the country. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/two-top-jjmp-naxals-killed-in-encounter-in-jharkhands-latehar/articleshow/121380268.cms (''Times of India'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Three of the four people on board are killed after a [[Bell 212]] [[police helicopter]] crashes and gets engulfed in flames in Nong Kok village, [[Prachuap Khiri Khan province]], [[Thailand]]. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/3033356/3-killed-in-police-helicopter-crash-in-prachuap-khiri-khan (''Bangkok Post'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Japan–North Korea relations]], [[North Korean abductions of Japanese citizens]]
**Families of [[Japanese people|Japanese citizens]] abducted by [[North Korea]] decades ago hold a rally in [[Tokyo]] to call on [[North Korean leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]] to return their relatives to Japan. [https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20250524/p2g/00m/0na/044000c (''The Mainichi'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*A power outage occurs during the [[2025 Cannes Film Festival]], which [[National Police (France)|French police]] later claim it was due to suspected [[arson]]. [https://apnews.com/article/cannes-film-power-outage-france-1747c2b19ae0eb92e5d7a6b21accdf68 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Daniel Noboa]] is sworn-in for his second consecutive term as [[President of Ecuador]]. [https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2025/05/24/daniel-noboa-toma-posesion-de-un-nuevo-mandato-como-presidente-de-ecuador/ (''Infobae'' <small>in Spanish)</small>]

'''Sports'''
*[[2024–25 Coupe de France]]
**In [[association football]], [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] wins a record 16th [[Coupe de France]] title after defeating [[Stade Reims]] 3–0 in [[2025 Coupe de France final|the final]] at the [[Stade de France]] in [[Saint-Denis, Seine-Saint-Denis|Saint-Denis]], [[Paris]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn8z037rrrlt (BBC Sport)]
*[[2024–25 Cypriot Cup]]
**In association football, [[AEK Larnaca]] win the [[Cypriot Cup]] after defeating [[Pafos FC]] on [[penalty shoot-out|penalties]] 5–4 after a 0–0 draw at the [[GSP Stadium]] in [[Nicosia]]. [https://www.cna.org.cy/en/article/8513188/aek-larnaca-secures-football-cup-title-following-a-penalty-shoot-out (Cyprus News Agency)]
*[[2024–25 DFB-Pokal]]
**In association football, [[VfB Stuttgart]] win the [[DFB-Pokal|German Cup]] after defeating [[Arminia Bielefeld]] 4–2 in [[2025 DFB-Pokal final|the final]] at [[Olympiastadion (Berlin)|Olympiastadion]] in [[Berlin]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c4g2rn799vet (BBC Sport)]
*[[2024–25 EFL Championship]]
**In association football, [[Sunderland AFC]] defeats [[Sheffield United]] 2–1 in [[stoppage time]] to win the [[English Football League]] [[English Football League play-offs|play-off]] [[2025 EFL Championship play-off final|final]] at [[Wembley Stadium]] in [[Wembley]], [[London]], and are [[promotion and relegation|promoted]] to the [[Premier League]] after an 8-year absence as a result. [https://www.skysports.com/football/sheff-utd-vs-sunderland/report/529582 (Sky Sports)] [https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/may/24/sunderland-promoted-to-premier-league-championship-playoff-final-sheffield-united (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2024–25 Ekstraklasa]]
**In association football, [[Lech Poznań]] wins their 9th [[Ekstraklasa]] title on the last day of the season after defeating [[Piast Gliwice]] 1–0 at home. [https://www.polsatsport.pl/wiadomosc/2025-05-24/lech-poznan-mistrze-polski/ (Polsat Sport <small>in Polish</small>)]
*[[2024–25 European Rugby Champions Cup]]
**In [[rugby union]], [[Bordeaux Bègles]] defeat the [[Northampton Saints]] 28–20 in [[2025 European Rugby Champions Cup final|the final]] to win the [[European Rugby Champions Cup]] at the [[Millennium Stadium]] in [[Cardiff]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/rugby-union/articles/c9vgd008jppo (BBC Sport)]
*[[2024–25 Nemzeti Bajnokság I]]
**In association football, state-backed [[Ferencvárosi TC|Ferencváros]] win their 36th overall and 7th consecutive [[Nemzeti Bajnokság I|league]] title after defeating [[ETO Győr]] 2–1 on the final day of the season. [https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/may/28/ferencvaros-puskas-akademia-vie-sporting-political-success (The Guardian)]
*[[2024–25 Scottish Cup]]
**In association football, [[Aberdeen F.C.]] wins their 9th [[Scottish Cup]] and their first in 35 years after defeating 42-time winners [[Celtic F.C.]] 4–3 in [[2025 Scottish Cup final|the final]] on penalties after a 1–1 draw at [[Hampden Park]] in [[Glasgow]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c2kqvl8g1x1t (BBC Sport)]
*[[2024–25 UEFA Women's Champions League]]
**In [[women's association football]], [[Arsenal W.F.C.|Arsenal]] wins the [[UEFA Women's Champions League]] for the second time after defeating [[FC Barcelona Femení|FC Barcelona]] 1–0 in [[2025 UEFA Women's Champions League final|the final]] played at the [[Estádio José Alvalade]] in [[Lisbon]], [[Portugal]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cy750rjxyy2t (BBC Sport)]
